public_rationale: The required conversion event is unverified. The engineering research addresses lifecycle costs, not completed conversions or investment written off. It therefore establishes neither the claimed necessity nor a decisive counterexample. The conditional-forecast rule prevents scoring while the antecedent remains unknown.
limitations: Failure to locate a conversion does not establish that none occurred.
A financial verdict would also require a defined investment scope and accounting basis.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Adapting AI data centers to other uses would require gutting them, wasting most of their capital expenditure.

statement.excerpt: Adapting them to other uses would require gutting the data center, which would mean that the vast majority of the capital expenditures were wasted.

from_speaker: would require gutting the data center
the vast majority of the capital expenditures were wasted
our_interpretation: Other uses means useful non-AI computing, including conventional hosting or scientific computing.
Gutting means removing or replacing most major installed systems, rather than changing software or replacing selected equipment.
Wasted capital means original investment rendered economically unusable by conversion, accounting for retained assets and recoverable equipment value.
The claim states a general necessity. One expensive conversion would not establish that all practical conversions require it.
No particular company, accounting basis, conversion date, or numerical meaning of vast majority is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: Completed conversions and applicable engineering constraints establish that practical non-AI reuse requires removing most major systems and losing an overwhelming share of original investment.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented, relevant conversion achieves useful non-AI operation while retaining major installed systems and a majority of original investment value.
